key_insight: Charge separation in low-offset organic solar cells is governed not just by the LE–CT energy gap, but also by state degeneracy and energetic disorder, which can either hinder or enhance efficiency depending on the offset regime.
engineering_relevance: Device design can target near-zero or even negative offsets if disorder-driven thermalization is leveraged, reducing the need for a large energetic driving force in organic photovoltaic blends.
method: Compared a macroscopic two-state rate model with 3D kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations
Analyzed charge separation across the full range of LE–CT energetic offsets
Tested the impact of Gaussian energetic disorder on internal quantum efficiency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the rate model matches kMC without disorder across all offsets, and kMC shows a crossover where disorder becomes beneficial at intermediate and low offsets but detrimental at large offsets.
watch_item: The beneficial effect of disorder depends on the specific offset regime and may not generalize to all material systems or processing conditions without careful calibration.
paper_title: Dependence of charge separation efficiency on the exciton-charge transfer offset and Gaussian disorder in organic solar cells
